header: Admin strings of the E42 design set, once each, by key. Slice 1 keys these; the parents' other quoted strings on D03:764-780, D04:778-787 and D05:817-824 join in slice 2. `entries` maps `SOURCE KEY` to the string: SOURCE is the parent line the string stands on (`D03:760` …) or, for a label this pack keys where no parent line names the control, the parent alone (`D03`). A key in `proposed` is authored here (PROPOSED, E42-D06): its value is the quoted parent literal that names the control, verbatim on SOURCE, or a note; `derived` says how a proposed string is built from its literal. `variants` lists a parent's other forms of a string (each on SOURCE too). `security` holds what breaks if a frozen string (E42-D06 §7.2) is reworded; a key not there is `none`. `conflict` names the F-row of a key two parents word differently. `retired` marks a parent string of a surface that does not ship (the ruling of record, comment 6608091305): it stays listed so that no build revives it. `inherited` keys belong to their owner and are never restated. The check (`docs/design/_tools/e42_d06_handoff_check.py`) re-reads every `entries` and `variants` string and every quoted literal on its source line; a string that opens a quoted literal there must close it whole (its quotes paired).

entries.D04:779 tamper.failed.meaning: Each record is linked to the one before it, so a change or gap shows here. The links are not keyed: someone with database access could also have rewritten earlier records consistently, so treat the whole log as unverified until security has compared it with an independent copy.

entries.D04:779 tamper.failed.steps: Don't change or delete anything in the database. Snapshot it, find the first broken link in the verifier log and escalate it as a security incident (SECURITY.md). Tell the security reviewer now.

security.admin.live_gate: a reason naming a settings toggle invites a bypass of the live gate
security.backup.dl.warning: a link not marked secret gets forwarded; it carries encrypted secrets
security.dlg.delete: SC-1: understating Delete hides that the name is anonymised after 90 days and becomes irreversible
security.dlg.flag.body: SC-5: dropping the override count hides who keeps the old value
security.dlg.maint_on.positions: an implied close misleads on what maintenance does to positions
security.export.dlg.pii: dropping it hides that the file holds personal data
security.flags.applied: SC-5: a longer or vaguer delay misstates the contract's 2 seconds
security.inv.close_warning: dropping it loses the only copy of the link
security.inv.once: a link not marked secret gets forwarded as a bearer credential
security.labels.unbind_a: SC-2: a choice name that drops "you take over" hides who manages the open positions
security.labels.unbind_b: SC-2: a choice name that drops "first" hides that access stays until the account is flat
security.notice.tightening: SC-2: a tightening that implies closing positions invites a manual flatten
security.onboard.secret_once: implying the secret can be viewed later invites storing it elsewhere
security.restore.confirm.stepup: condition 4 and SC-3: dropping "spends the code" misleads on the refusal's cost
security.restore.impact.bybit: SC-3: a restore that seems to touch Bybit, or to stop live orders, misleads on exchange exposure
security.restore.impact.market: SC-3: implying market history returns hides a data gap
security.restore.impact.rewind: condition 1: a softer word than "replaced" implies a reversal only a prior backup gives
security.restore.impact.signin: SC-3: hiding the credential rollback misleads on who can sign in afterwards
security.restore.impact.trading: SC-3: dropping "stays off until you turn it back on" implies trading resumes by itself
security.restore.positions.open: SC-3 and condition 3: the count spans demo and live; naming one environment understates it
security.restore.positions.unknown: SC-3: dropping "doesn't change anything on Bybit" removes the acknowledged fact
security.tamper.failed.safe: dropping it hides the kill switch IR-06 names
security.tamper.failed.title: a softer headline turns a security incident into a UI error
security.unbind.a: SC-2: dropping the stop-loss sentence reads as an unprotected position
security.unbind.ack: SC-2: the acknowledgement is what the contract records; softening it records less than was accepted
security.unbind.b: SC-2: dropping the counts hides how much closes at market
security.unbind.b_option_a: SC-2: dropping it promises a removal that a failed close does not deliver
security.va.entry.notice: a reason disclosed to the target, or a notice implied when none is sent, misstates privacy
